But open Grandma's jar of jam

why.en: The frost has emptied the orchard, 'But' the jar of jam holds 'summer': heat, bees, light. A thing made in summer keeps its feeling. No recipe, loss or beekeeping.
why.uz: Ayoz bogʻni boʻshatgan, «But» murabbo bankasida yoz bor: issiqlik, asalarilar, yorugʻlik. Sheʼr yozda qilingan narsa yoz hissini saqlashini koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Мороз опустошил сад, «But» в банке варенья — лето: жара, пчёлы, свет. Сделанное летом хранит его ощущение. Ни рецепта, ни утраты, ни пчеловодства.

But scores can rise for many reasons: an easier test, a stronger group of students, a new teacher who joined the same year. Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

It describes a new reading program and then lists the many reasons that students enjoy it.

stem.en:
It is easy to assume that a desert holds little life, because at midday almost nothing moves. But many desert animals avoid the heat by resting underground during the day and coming out only after sunset. A visitor who walks the same sand at night with a torch finds tracks, beetles and the quick shadow of a jerboa where the afternoon showed only stillness.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To show that a desert seems empty because of when it is seen, not for lack of life
To describe how jerboas dig the deep burrows that keep them cool during the hottest hours
To warn visitors about the dangers of walking in the desert at night
To explain why desert sand cools quickly after the sun goes down

why.en: Sentence 1 states an assumption; 'But' explains that animals hide by day; the night walk shows life where the afternoon showed none. The jerboa is one detail, not the purpose.
why.uz: 1-gap — taxmin; «But» hayvonlar kunduzi yashirinishini tushuntiradi; tungi sayr kunduzi koʻrinmagan hayotni koʻrsatadi. Qoʻshoyoq — bir tafsilot, maqsad emas.
why.ru: 1-е — допущение; «But» объясняет, что звери прячутся днём; ночная прогулка показывает жизнь там, где днём было пусто. Тушканчик — деталь, а не цель.

stem.en:

Older farmers in the valley still predict the weather by signs: swallows flying low, a ring around the moon, the smell of the morning wind. Such signs, some say, are mere superstition and should give way to the forecast on the phone.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view in Text 1 that the farmers' signs are "mere superstition"?

By agreeing that every old sign should give way to the phone forecast
By claiming that all of the farmers' signs are more accurate than any phone forecast
By suggesting that swallows cause the damp air that comes before rain

why.en: Text 2 shows that low swallows follow damp air before rain, so 'a sign can be old without being false'; it asks which signs follow the weather: judge each one, not all at once.
why.uz: 2-matn past uchgan qaldirgʻochlar yomgʻir oldidan nam havoga ergashishini koʻrsatadi: «a sign can be old without being false». Har bir belgini alohida baholash kerak.

Steel bridges last much longer than the old bridges that were built of stone.
Bridges grow a little shorter every year as they get older.
Engineers must close the gaps in a steel bridge each winter.

The students closed the old drain from the town's market.
The river smelled bad only after the factory had closed.

Onions make people cry because cutting one breaks open tiny cells and releases a gas that stings the eyes. Many cooks have their own tricks. Chilling the onion in the refrigerator before cutting it slows the release of the gas, and a very sharp knife crushes fewer cells than a dull one, so less gas escapes.

According to the text, why does a sharp knife help?

It cuts the onion faster than the gas can reach the eyes.
It keeps the onion cold while the cook is cutting it.
It removes the part of the onion that holds the gas.

The potter plans to start making his bowls with a machine next year.

A city's famous buildings are visited mostly by tourists rather than by the people who live there.
Most residents of the city plan to move away within a few years.
Postcards of a city give an accurate picture of how its residents live.

stem.en:
Many people picture a forest fire as pure destruction. In some dry woodlands, however, fire has long been part of the forest's life. Certain pine cones open and release their seeds only after intense heat, and the ash left behind returns minerals to the soil. Putting out every small fire can even backfire: dead wood piles up year after year, so that when a fire finally comes, it burns far hotter than the forest can survive.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: In some forests fire has a natural role, and stopping every fire can do harm.
All pine cones need the heat of a forest fire before they can release their seeds.
Forest fires should be started on purpose every summer in dry woodlands.
The ash left by a fire makes the soil too poor for new trees to grow.

why.en: The text shows fire helping some forests (seeds, minerals) and says stopping every small fire lets dead wood pile up for a worse fire. 'All' cones and fires 'every summer' go too far.
why.uz: Matn olov baʼzi oʻrmonlarga foyda berishini (urugʻ, minerallar) va har bir kichik yongʻinni oʻchirish quruq yogʻoch yigʻib, battar yongʻinga olib kelishini aytadi. «All» — ortiqcha.

When the river later shifted its course to the west, the bazaar stayed where it was, even though the reason for its location had disappeared.

The town center was too crowded to hold a large market.
Merchants wanted to stay far from the river's spring floods.
The river had shifted west, leaving open land beside the town.

stem.en:
In a poem, the speaker describes the bazaar early in the morning as quiet and still waking up.

Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates this description?

options.en: "The stalls stand shuttered, half asleep; / a single broom sweeps by the gate."
"By noon the crowd is loud and thick, / and every seller shouts a price above the rest."
"My mother buys the reddest plums / and lets me carry home the heavy bag."
"The melon man is old and kind / and gives the children slices free."

why.en: The description has two parts: quiet, and still waking. 'Shuttered, half asleep' with one broom shows both; the noon crowd is the opposite, and the rest are not about morning.
why.uz: Tavsif ikki qismli: sokin va hali uygʻonayotgan. «Shuttered, half asleep» va bitta supurgi ikkalasini koʻrsatadi; tush paytidagi olomon — aksi, qolganlari tong haqida emas.
why.ru: В описании две части: тишина и пробуждение. «Shuttered, half asleep» и одна метла показывают обе; полуденная толпа — наоборот, остальное не об утре.

stem.en:
After the school canteen began playing soft music at lunch, the canteen manager noticed that students left less food on their plates. She concluded that the music made students enjoy their meals more and eat more of them.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the manager's conclusion?

options.en: In the same week the music began, the canteen also started serving smaller portions.
Students said that they liked the songs that the canteen played at lunch more than silence.
The music is played only during the lunch hour, never at breakfast.
Students who eat in the canteen usually stay for about twenty minutes.

why.en: Smaller portions starting the same week could explain the cleaner plates without the music. Students liking the songs, if anything, fits her view.
why.uz: Oʻsha haftada porsiyalar kichraygani tozaroq likopchalarni musiqasiz ham tushuntiradi. Oʻquvchilarga qoʻshiqlar yoqqani esa uning fikriga mos keladi.
why.ru: Уменьшение порций в ту же неделю объясняет чистые тарелки без музыки. А то, что песни нравятся ученикам, скорее согласуется с её выводом.

stem.en:
In a short story, Komil is a shy boy who slowly gains confidence. An essay about the story argues that in its final scene, Komil is ready to speak in front of others.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates the essay's argument?

options.en: "When the teacher asked who would read the class letter aloud at the assembly, Komil raised his hand at once."
"Komil usually sat at the back of the room, where he hoped no teacher would ever call on him to answer a question."
"Komil wrote long letters to his cousin but never showed them to anyone else."
"At home, Komil often helped his mother bake bread for the neighbors."

why.en: The essay is about speaking before others in the last scene. Only volunteering to read aloud at the assembly shows that; sitting at the back shows his shyness at the start.
why.uz: Insho oxirgi sahnada boshqalar oldida gapirishga tayyorlik haqida. Buni faqat yigʻilishda ovoz chiqarib oʻqishga qoʻl koʻtarish koʻrsatadi; orqada oʻtirish — boshidagi uyatchanlik.
why.ru: Эссе — о готовности говорить перед другими в финальной сцене. Это показывает только то, что он сам вызвался читать вслух на линейке; задняя парта — его робость в начале.

stem.en:
Members of a youth hiking club noticed that groups who set off before seven in the morning finished the mountain trail with fewer people turning back. The club leader, Davron, suggests that starting early helps hikers avoid the midday heat, which tires them out.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Davron's suggestion?

options.en: On cloudy, cool days, groups that started late finished the trail as often as early groups.
Most club members prefer to hike with friends rather than to hike alone.
The early groups carried more water with them than the late groups did.
The club plans to open a second, easier mountain trail for its youngest members next spring.

why.en: If late groups do just as well when there is no heat, the heat, not the hour, explains the difference, as Davron says. More water in early groups would point to another cause.
why.uz: Issiq boʻlmagan kunlarda kech chiqqanlar ham xuddi shunday yaxshi oʻtsa, farqni vaqt emas, issiq tushuntiradi. Erta chiqqan guruhlarda suv koʻproq boʻlishi boshqa sababga ishora qiladi.
why.ru: Если в прохладные дни поздние группы проходят так же, разницу объясняет жара, а не время выхода, как и говорит Даврон. Больше воды у ранних групп указывало бы на иную причину.

stem.en:
A city's transport office reports that since a new metro line opened, the traffic jams on the main avenue above it have become shorter. The office concludes that many drivers have switched from their cars to the metro.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the office's conclusion?

options.en: Over the same months, a new ring road opened, drawing many drivers away from the avenue.
The new metro line carries many passengers on weekday mornings.
A metro ticket costs much less than the fuel that a car needs for the same trip across the city.
Traffic jams on the avenue are still longest on Friday evenings.

why.en: If drivers left the avenue for a new ring road, shorter jams need not mean that they took the metro. Busy trains and cheap tickets, if anything, fit the office's view.
why.uz: Agar haydovchilar yangi halqa yoʻliga oʻtgan boʻlsa, tirbandlik qisqarishi ular metroga oʻtganini bildirmaydi. Gavjum poyezd va arzon chipta esa idoraning fikriga mos.
why.ru: Если водители ушли на новую кольцевую, сокращение пробок не значит, что они пересели в метро. Полные поезда и дешёвые билеты скорее подтверждают вывод.

stem.en:
In a short story, the narrator's aunt runs a small sewing workshop. The narrator claims that the aunt's strictness with her apprentices hides real care for them.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates the narrator's claim?

options.en: "She made them unpick a crooked seam three times, then stayed late to teach the slowest girl the stitch again, alone."
"She never allowed tea at the cutting table, and she checked every single seam herself, holding each dress up to the light."
"Her apprentices called her kind and gentle, and she never once raised her voice at any of them."
"She kept the workshop open until late every evening so that the wedding orders were finished on time."

why.en: The claim needs strictness and hidden care: three unpickings are strict, staying late to teach the slowest girl is care. The tea rule shows only strictness.
why.uz: Daʼvoga qattiqlik va yashirin gʻamxoʻrlik kerak: chokni uch marta soʻktirish — qattiqlik, eng sekin qizga ishdan keyin oʻrgatish — gʻamxoʻrlik. Choy qoidasi faqat qattiqlikni koʻrsatadi.
why.ru: Нужны строгость и скрытая забота: трижды распороть шов — строго, остаться учить отстающую — забота. Запрет на чай показывает только строгость.

stem.en:
Saida noticed that the bread her grandmother bakes in the clay tandir stays fresh longer than bread from the electric oven, even when both are made from the same dough. Saida hypothesizes that the tandir's very high heat forms a thicker crust, which keeps moisture inside the loaf.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Saida's hypothesis?

options.en: Oven loaves baked at the highest heat grew thicker crusts and stayed fresh as long as tandir bread.
Loaves from the tandir were always eaten much more quickly by the family than loaves from the oven.
Her grandmother shapes the tandir bread by hand, while the oven bread is shaped in a metal pan.
Most neighbors said that the two kinds of bread tasted exactly the same.

why.en: If high heat alone gives oven bread a thick crust and the same long freshness, heat and crust explain it, as Saida says. A difference in shaping would point elsewhere.
why.uz: Agar faqat yuqori harorat pechdagi nonga qalin qobiq bersa va bu non ham tandir nonidek uzoq yangi tursa, buni Saida aytgandek issiqlik va qobiq tushuntiradi. Shakl farqi boshqa sababga ishora qiladi.
why.ru: Если одна лишь высокая температура даёт хлебу из духовки толстую корку и ту же свежесть, дело в жаре и корке, как и думает Саида. Разная форма указала бы на другое.

The family made 7 jars of quince jam and 4 jars of fig jam.

The club leader concluded that although more tickets were sold for Saturday, a larger share of the seats was filled on Friday.

someone had opened the bag during the drive and blown into it.
the crisps inside had grown larger in the cold mountain air.

the one filled with plain tap water.
the one that held more water.
the one standing in the warmer spot.

why.en: Salt water freezes at a lower temperature, so on a night cold enough to freeze tap water, the salty dish could stay liquid. The dishes stood side by side.

caused by the autumn rains.
present in the well water all year round.

the town's builders never learned how to fire bricks of their own.
the river stones were brought to the town from distant mountains.
the brick houses were built before the houses of river stone.

the pale ones, which birds will find harder to see on the blackened bark.
the ones that rest on the ground instead of on the trees.
the moths of both forms equally, since birds hunt by sight.

Zulfiya noticed that her pilaf turned out sticky whenever she cooked it in her large pot but fluffy in her small pot. She blamed the large pot until she realized something else: she used the large pot only for guests, and before those big meals, to save time, she skipped rinsing the rice. To find out whether the pot itself matters, she should most logically ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: cook a large batch in the large pot with rice she has rinsed.
cook a small batch in the small pot with rice she has rinsed.
stop cooking pilaf for guests in either of her pots.
buy a second small pot to use for the big meals.

why.en: The pot and the rinsing changed together. Using the large pot with rinsed rice changes only the pot; the small pot with rinsed rice is what she already does.

stem.en:
A river carries mud down from the mountains. Where the water flows fast, the mud is swept along; where the water slows, the mud sinks to the bottom. Where the river leaves its narrow mountain valley, it spreads out wide and shallow, and over thousands of years a broad, flat plain of rich soil has formed there. The plain most likely formed because ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the river slowed there and dropped the mud it carried.
the river flows fastest at the place where it leaves the mountains.
the mountains near the plain are made of soil rather than rock.
farmers carried mud to that place over many years.

why.en: Mud sinks where the water slows, and where the river spreads out wide and shallow it slows, so it drops its mud there, building the plain.
